So we're going to take $1, $1, and we're going to divide that by our stop-loss percent. Now, in this case, we have a 2% stop loss. So 2% becomes 0.02. 02 and that's going to equal the amount of dollars that we put on the trade. Now, if we take $1 and we divide this by 0.02, that's going to equal $50. Now, this we don't really need to do the calculation for this one because a 2% stop-loss, you know, you put half of your account on the trade and after half your account goes down 2%, that's a 1% loss. So, we would plan this trade. We say, 'Okay, I'm planning for this trade. I know I'm risking $1. So, because I have a 2% stop-loss, I'm going to put $50 on the trade. And then, of course, you know, if this trade gets stopped out here, we're risking $1. If it pumps up in this instance, this is like a six to1 riskreward. We're either going to lose $1 or we're going to make $6 and we're going to put $50 on the trade. Now, notice this. We're putting $50 on the trade while only risking $1.
